summary.headline: Mrs. Bectors Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR548.7 crores with EBITDA margin at 13.1%, targeting 14% by Q4.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to INR548.7 crores and 12.9% QoQ, with exports reported as high-double-digit growth. EBITDA rose 23.8% to INR72.1 crores, margin up 80 bps YoY to 13.1%, and PAT rose 25.5% to INR38.8 crores. Management said price increases and Project IMPACT largely offset input cost inflation in Q1, but expects Q2 to be the most challenging quarter for commodity and packaging costs. Full-year guidance is mid-teens revenue growth and a 14% EBITDA margin by Q4, with about 16% targeted by FY30.

segments.name: Biscuits (Cremica)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR325 crores, up 15.7% YoY; domestic biscuit sales grew high-single digits on both price and volume. Management said biscuit EBITDA margin is slightly below company average.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, Naturbaked, QSR)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR215 crores, up 17.5% YoY; Naturbaked crossed a monthly revenue run rate of INR1 crore. Bakery EBITDA margin is above company average; B2B/QSR returned to good double-digit growth.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew at high-double-digit rate; volume-led. Export contribution is about 35% of revenue; US contribution is about 23-25% per management, and US is back on growth after tariff-related slowdown.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Grew 58% YoY per management; Kolkata bakery unit (commissioned Q4 FY26) now serving East markets.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth targeted at mid-teens (about 17-19% cited in Q&A context); biscuits low-teens, bakery low-teens, exports close to mid-teens.
EBITDA margin target of 14% in Q4 FY27; Q2 expected to see the sharpest commodity and packaging impact, Q3 fully covered by pricing and cost actions.
Project IMPACT expected to deliver about 0.4-0.5% cost benefit this year.
Medium term: EBITDA closer to 16% (15-16%) by FY30 with revenue target of INR4,000 crores.
Consumer price increases of about 2-2.5% taken during Q1, with the balance of the impact in Q2; Q1 inflation impact about 1.5%.
capex_capacity: Capex this year covering existing and in-progress projects could reach about INR3,400-3,500 crores at current prices, per management; excludes Bangalore.
Bangalore plant: shortlisted location; this year's new investment approx INR200 crores beyond last year's spillover; machine orders still being finalised.
Khopoli (Maharashtra) plant commissioned March 2026, stabilising; Kolkata unit commissioned Q4 FY26 (about INR20 crores).
MP plant opened mainly for exports (closer to port) with fiscal incentive; now starting central-market distribution.
Capex funding: about 60% from internal accruals and 40% borrowings this year.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand healthy across retail and institutional; consumption better than feared at last call.
Competition intense in biscuits, especially Upper North India; company stepped up trade promotion and marketing spend.
Plan to add 40,000 billed outlets above INR200/outlet (about 12-13% increase in billed outlets).
Export orders are month-to-month, not a long order book; management said no restocking benefit in Q1.
Inflation impact about 1-2% over last year; contract manufacturing about 1-1.5% of revenue.
Domestic general trade split roughly 50% Upper North and 50% Rest of India; English Oven revenue about 80% North India, with upcountry and NCR now roughly equal.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic biscuit growth and mix of price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: High-single-digit growth, with both pricing and volume contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is the toughest quarter for commodity costs; Q3 fully covered by pricing and cost actions; 14% EBITDA targeted by Q4 and about 16% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Is export growth driven by restocking or one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no restocking; growth is from new SKUs (e.g., peanut butter cracker at Walmart) and projects that resumed after US tariff slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly freight and fuel (plant fuel consumption) plus higher marketing and trade promotion spend.

qa_highlights.question: Excise/export incentives status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government incentives have not yet materialised; importers pay destination duties. New Zealand FTA and UK are emerging markets.

qa_highlights.question: Capex run rate beyond current cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports about INR3,500 crores revenue at current prices, plus Bangalore; more capacity to be added as business grows; funding 60% internal.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 margin pressure from commodity, packaging and freight costs; management expects only partial recovery in Q2.
Escalation of West Asia conflict, vessel availability and freight costs affecting exports.
Intense competition in Upper North biscuits; sustained elevated marketing and trade spend may weigh on margins.
Execution of Bangalore and wider capacity expansion, and funding mix (40% borrowings in FY27).
Management did not disclose domestic biscuit segment margin; delivery of 14% Q4 target depends on pricing pass-through and Project IMPACT.
Reiterated revenue expectations (mid-teens growth) vs Q1 high-teens growth; seasonality cited.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q1 execution and margin trajectory, but cautious on Q2 cost pressure and the West Asia situation. Management was evasive on segment-level margin for domestic biscuits and on export duty/incentive details.
key_quotes: Importantly, the growth was accompanied by margin expansion.
So quarter 2 could be a quarter where we will be able to cover most of it, not entirely, but quarter 3, again, we will be fully covered.
Naturbaked has crossed a monthly revenue rate of INR1 crore.
So over a period of next 3 to 4 years, say, by 2030 financial year, we want to hit EBITDA closer to 16%.

adds.what: Kolkata bakery unit now serving East markets
MP plant opened mainly for exports, starting central-market distribution
Bangalore plant: shortlisted location, machine orders being finalised; approx INR200 crore new investment this year

growth.why: Management targets mid-teens FY27 revenue growth (17-19% cited in Q&A) backed by price increases, Project IMPACT (0.4-0.5% cost benefit), new Khopoli/Kolkata/MP capacity and a 40,000-outlet expansion, while Q1 revenue grew 16% YoY and EBITDA grew 23.8%; Bangalore capacity is only at shortlist stage and not yet live.
